lines: Boots dusty, soles whole. That is how I like returning.
Home looks better after a road that long.
You kept your word and brought me back safely.
I checked every strap before we left, and not one failed us.
The journey was tiring, but it never felt careless.
I would travel with you again after a few quiet days here.
We chose good places to rest. That mattered more than I expected.
My pack came home lighter and my trust came home stronger.
You warned me before the road became dangerous.
The boots need oil, but my feet are still in them.
I learned how far I can walk without slowing everyone down.
We had enough food because someone actually planned ahead.
The village bell was the finest sound on the return.
I kept waiting for the trip to turn ugly. It never did.
You noticed when I needed rest before I had to ask.
Even the rain found us prepared.
I have a few repairs to make and no wounds to hide.
The road taught me that sensible company is worth the extra pace.
Next time I will carry less thread and more supper.
Thank you for making the journey feel like travel instead of escape.
I can patch leather. Patching myself is worse work.
The road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
This bandage pulls whenever I reach for the awl.
I remember the hit more clearly than the miles before it.
You got me home, but we should not pretend the plan was good.
My boot held after my ankle stopped cooperating.
I had to cut a strap apart to bind the wound.
We waited too long before looking for shelter.
The cleric says I will heal. I still intend to complain.
I could not carry my own pack for the last stretch.
The blood came out of the leather more easily than I expected.
I should have spoken when the pain first started.
We need a better way to retreat when someone is hurt.
Every bump in the road home found the same bruise.
I am grateful you did not leave me behind.
Do not ask me to walk that route again until the swelling is gone.
My tools feel heavier with one hand wrapped.
The injury will mend, but I learned where our plan failed.
If there is a next journey, we pack bandages where they can be reached.
You split trust like old hide. It will not soften quickly.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
I keep replaying the moment you turned on me.
You knew I had nowhere safe to run.
Do not speak of the journey as if we shared it honestly.
I repaired the pack you abandoned. The trust is harder work.
My wounds closed before I could understand why you caused them.
You watched me follow and used that against me.
I will not travel beyond the village with you again.
An apology does not erase a trap set by someone I trusted.
I should not have needed to guard my back from my own guide.
The road home gave me plenty of time to remember your choice.
You can return what you took. It will not return what we had.
I know now which promises from you cannot bear weight.
Do not mistake this conversation for forgiveness.
Others may trust you again. I am not ready.
The worst part was realizing the danger had been beside me all along.
I survived your decision, but I will carry it for a while.
If you want to repair this, start by giving me distance.
Boat spray is poor treatment for leather. Better than swimming, though.
The boat did its part. I am still judging the rest of the plan.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
My pack stayed dry until the last wave found it.
I spent half the crossing holding a loose seat in place.
Next time, we check the oars before pushing away from shore.
The wind changed faster than our little boat could turn.
I have salt drying in every seam I wore.
You handled the current better than I handled the rocking.
The shore looked close until we tried to reach it.
I never want to hear water slosh under the floor again.
We should bring a cover for the supplies on the next crossing.
The boat scraped bottom twice near the reeds.
I was relieved when the road continued on solid ground.
One buckle has already started rusting from that spray.
We saw more drowned than I wanted to count.
I would still choose that boat over the distance we would have walked.
The calm stretch in the middle almost made the trip pleasant.
I know now which gear belongs in a waxed bundle.
If we travel by water again, I am sitting farther from the leaking side.
